name: Bilbao
tagline: Postwar pintxos, txangurro like always, and a Michelin star inside the Guggenheim.

Víctor Montes.description: Started as a grocery store in 1849 and is today the emblem of pintxos in Plaza Nueva, in the Old Town.

A Mina.description: Product-driven cuisine from chef Álvaro Garrido by the estuary, on Paseo de Marzana. One Michelin star.

Zarate.description: A temple of grilled fish and seasonal shellfish. One Michelin star.

Nerua Guggenheim Bilbao.description: Contemporary Basque haute cuisine inside the Guggenheim Museum itself. One Michelin star.

El Globo.description: Its gratinated txangurro pintxo is an absolute classic, next to the Provincial Council Palace.

La Olla.description: Rice dishes, grilled chuletón steak, and a secret art deco bathtub nook that went viral on TikTok, right on Plaza Nueva.

Ola Martín Berasategui.description: Martín Berasategui's signature restaurant in the heart of the Old Town, with Raúl Cabrera leading the kitchen. One Michelin star.

Islares.description: Bilbao's newest addition to the 2026 Michelin Guide, from chef Julen Bergantiños. One Michelin star.

Charly.description: A pintxos bar open since 1973, one of the most respected in the Old Town.

Gure Toki.description: Avant-garde pintxos rooted in Basque tradition, on Plaza Nueva.

Mercado de la Ribera.description: One of the largest covered markets in Europe, on the banks of the estuary, with pintxos stalls and fresh produce.

Bar Berton.description: A go-to pintxos bar on Calle Jardines in the Old Town, prized for the quality of its ingredients and its hot, chef-driven pintxos.

Café Iruña.description: Historic café opened in 1903 facing the Jardines de Albia, with a Mudéjar-style hall decorated by architect Joaquín Rucoba; a meeting point for Unamuno and other Basque intellectuals.

La Viña del Ensanche.description: A Bilbao institution since 1927 specializing in Joselito acorn-fed Ibérico ham and vermouth, on the Ensanche's Calle Diputación.

Restaurante Guria.description: A cathedral of salt cod founded by the Pildain family in 1948, now on Gran Vía after the 1983 flood; Jenaro Pildain was considered the king of Basque cod.

Zortziko.description: Chef Daniel García's haute-cuisine restaurant near the Guggenheim, which held a Michelin star for more than thirty consecutive years until the chef's retirement.

Atelier Etxanobe.description: Chef Fernando Canales moved his gastronomic kitchen to central Bilbao after nineteen years at the Euskalduna Palace. One Michelin star.

La Despensa del Etxanobe.description: The more casual side of Fernando Canales and Mikel Población, in the same building as the Atelier, serving reimagined traditional Basque cuisine.

Bar Gatz.description: Open since 1994 on Calle Santa María, it was one of the first bars -not restaurants- to appear in the Michelin Guide; its bacalao al pil-pil is the most-ordered pintxo.

Xukela.description: A landmark of the Old Town since 1982 on Calle del Perro, known for its prepared vermouth and lively atmosphere.

Rio-Oja.description: Open since 1959 on Calle del Perro, it serves homemade stews ladled straight from big pots at the bar instead of pintxos.

Casa Rufo.description: A grocery store founded in 1955 that gave rise in 1995 to this restaurant of chargrilled chuletón and a full wine cellar.

Bascook.description: Chef-driven market cuisine in a former bank building in the Ensanche, with a creative, seasonal menu.

Marisquería Serantes.description: A go-to seafood restaurant in Bilbao since the 1980s, with several locations across the city serving the freshest shellfish and fish.

Txintxirri Taberna.description: A small tavern steps from the Guggenheim and the Isozaki Towers, known for its potato omelette and classic pintxos.

El Puertito.description: Bilbao's first oyster bar, opened in 2013 on Calle García Rivero, with oysters from France, Galicia and Holland paired with txakoli.

Sorginzulo.description: Avant-garde pintxos made to order by chef Iñaki Lazkano on Plaza Nueva, with more than 25 years in the trade.

Santa María Taberna.description: A tavern with 1960s décor on Calle Santa María, famous for its foie pintxo with caramelized apple.

Pastelería Arrese.description: A pastry shop founded in 1852, famous for its carolinas, Basque sponge cake, and chocolate truffles, with a workshop on Calle Rodríguez Arias.

Aitor Rauleaga.description: Traditional Basque cooking and daily spoon-stews next to the old Hotel Abando, awarded a Repsol Sun.

Yandiola.description: Basque-rooted cuisine with a modern outlook from chef Ricardo Pérez Palacios, inside the Azkuna Zentroa building (the former Alhóndiga), with a panoramic terrace over Bilbao.

Bar Baster.description: A young, modern bar next to Santiago Cathedral, known for its gildas and freshly made omelettes.

Kerren Asador.description: Bilbao's oldest grill house, founded in 1978 by Inocencio Urigoitia in Indautxu, specializing in chargrilled chuletón.

Iturriza Taberna.description: A former religious-goods shop founded in 1885 on Plaza Nueva, now a pintxos tavern run by the third generation of the Iturriza family.

Basquery.description: A food space in the Ensanche combining a bakery, general store, its own craft brewery, and an aging chamber for Basque cheeses.

Bar Irrintzi.description: Elaborate, internationally inflected pintxos on Calle Santa María, with self-service in the heart of the Old Town's bar-hopping zone.

Café Bar Bilbao.description: Open since 1911 on Plaza Nueva, it keeps its original tiled décor and is one of the classic stops on the pintxos route.

Casa Vasca.description: A traditional Basque restaurant in the Deusto neighborhood, with more than four decades in business.

Bilbao Urban Sagardotegi.description: An urban cider house in the Ensanche recreating the txotx ritual with chuletón, salt cod, and cod omelette washed down with poured cider.

Los Fueros.description: A classic bar on Calle Fueros, in the heart of the Old Town, known above all for its popular txistorra pintxo.
